A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“retinal thinning” is a new objective measure of the efficacy of ocular nutrition.
“retinal thinning is the earliest objective sign of AMD and is a useful clinical marker of early AMD.”
“retinal thinning” in extrafoveal regions is a useful clinical metric for evaluating the effect of repletion of ocular nutrients in early AMD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retina in early AMD patients is not only vulnerable to thinning but also to functional visual loss.
the retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor cells are vulnerable to retinal atrophy in the superior and nasal retina of AMD patients.
the extrafoveal retinal layers are more vulnerable to AMD pathology than the central fovea.
